met:67.43.16.name: Paul E. Manheim
met:67.43.16.role: Donor named in the collection record
met:67.43.16.detail: Manheim’s 1967 gift explains the accession line. The separate record places the inscribed bone in the Shang period.

met:91.1.535a-h.name: ‘Umar ibn Yusuf
met:91.1.535a-h.role: Maker named in the instrument’s inscription
met:91.1.535a-h.detail: The Met reads the signature of the Rasulid prince and dates the instrument to 690 AH, given as 1291 CE. The catalogue also describes a reused plate and a modern pin.

bnf:coreen-109.name: Baegun
bnf:coreen-109.detail: The BnF names the Buddhist monk as the compiler. Its accession Coréen 109 identifies the second volume of the 1377 metal-type printing made at Heungdeok-sa in Cheongju.

henan:7052472642044956672.name: Juzhong Zhang
henan:7052472642044956672.role: Co-author of an archaeological report on the Jiahu flutes
henan:7052472642044956672.detail: Zhang and colleagues described excavated flutes and reported instrument tests. The Henan Museum identifies this featured 23.1 cm flute individually. Its maker’s name is unrecorded.

penn:b16665.name: Enheduanna
penn:b16665.detail: The Penn Museum reads Enheduanna’s name on the disk and identifies a scene in relief on its other face.

penn:b16665.name: Sargon
penn:b16665.detail: The Penn Museum’s description identifies Enheduanna as the daughter of Sargon of Akkad.

nmp:laguna-copperplate.name: Angkatan
nmp:laguna-copperplate.role: Recipient named in Postma’s published reading
nmp:laguna-copperplate.detail: The preliminary translation places Angkatan with her relative Bukah when the clearance was given.

nmp:laguna-copperplate.name: Namwran
nmp:laguna-copperplate.role: Person whose outstanding debt the document clears
nmp:laguna-copperplate.detail: Postma’s reading identifies Namwran and says the document safeguards the clearance against later claims.

nmp:laguna-copperplate.name: Kasumuran
nmp:laguna-copperplate.role: Witness named in Postma’s published reading
nmp:laguna-copperplate.detail: The preliminary translation names Kasumuran as leader of Puliran and places the clearance in his presence.

cma:2022.168.name: Seifū Yohei III
cma:2022.168.role: Maker credited in the collection record
cma:2022.168.detail: The museum connects the named maker, the underglaze blue begonias and the overglaze colours to this teapot and its accession.

cma:2022.206.name: Seifū Yohei IV
cma:2022.206.role: Maker credited in the collection record
cma:2022.206.detail: The museum attributes this sweets bowl to Seifū Yohei IV. Its record distinguishes the moulded part of the design from its in-glaze and underglaze colours.

cma:1966.500.10.name: Feodor Ivanovich Rückert
cma:1966.500.10.role: Workmaster credited in the collection record
cma:1966.500.10.detail: The museum names Rückert and the House of Fabergé for these sugar tongs. Opaque cloisonné enamel decorates the silver gilt.
